actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

facts.text: ECMReach-v0 is registered with entry point surrol.tasks.ecm_reach:ECMReach and max_episode_steps=50
The ECM action size is 3
The action space is a Box from -1.0 to 1.0 with one bound per action element
ECMReach selects the dmove action mode
In dmove mode the action is scaled by 0.01 and added to the RCM position, then sent through the ECM inverse kinematics
The ECMReach workspace limits are ((0.45, 0.55), (-0.05, 0.05), (0.60, 0.70))
A reset draws the goal uniformly from the workspace limits
The ECM starts at (0.45, 0.05, 0.70): the workspace lower x, upper y and upper z
The success threshold is 0.005 m: DISTANCE_THRESHOLD is 0.005 and SCALING is 1.0
The sparse reward is 0 on success and -1 otherwise: compute_reward is _is_success - 1
The observation is a Dict with the keys observation, achieved_goal and desired_goal
ECMReach sets has_object to False, so object_pos is empty and the observation vector is the 6-value robot state
The step returns (observation, reward, done, info) and done is always False
A reset rebuilds the scene, resamples the goal and returns the observation
EcmEnv sets the step duration to 0.1 s
SurRoLEnv.step advances the simulation by step(self._duration)
The simulation loop calls p.stepSimulation() int(duration * 240) times, i.e. 240 physics steps per simulated second
The environment's seed() stores numpy's generator and returns [seed]
The goal draw uses numpy's global random generator (np.random.rand)
The ECM has 4 degrees of freedom and its end-effector link index is 4

determinism.notes: reset(seed) reseeds the fake's random.Random and the kinematic step is deterministic, so one seed and one action sequence repeat a trajectory; upstream's seed() stores a numpy Generator that _sample_goal does not use (it draws from the global numpy RNG), so the fake's seeded goal stream is a stand-in, not upstream's

gaps: the upstream model is PyBullet rigid-body dynamics with contacts and ECM inverse kinematics (surrol/gym/surrol_env.py:93-119, surrol/tasks/ecm_env.py:125-145); this package's fake moves the end effector kinematically by action * 0.01 m and holds the orientation at zero, so its trajectories are not the upstream ones
no actuator, sensor or noise model is declared by the clone; the F1 claim stops at rigid-body dynamics with contacts and the model was never validated against a physical ECM
the sim backend (gym.make('ECMReach-v0') on the PyBullet environment) was not run where the gate ran; only the fake backend is checked
the seed path is a stand-in: upstream seed() stores numpy's generator but _sample_goal uses the global numpy RNG (surrol/tasks/ecm_reach.py:32), so the fake seeds its own random.Random instead

no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0 and lockstep; the physics timestep is 1000/240 ms (surrol/utils/pybullet_utils.py:18-20) and the control period is 100 ms: one env.step advances self._duration = 0.1 s, i.e. 24 physics steps (surrol/tasks/ecm_env.py:48, surrol/gym/surrol_env.py:102); one bridge tick is one env.step, and the fake advances that 100 ms transition without modelling the substeps
snapshot and restore are not offered: the upstream environment exposes no get_state/set_state
the fake loads no URDF assets and offers no rendering

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: after an e-stop no step or reset is accepted until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the last observation and tick stay readable
